title: Cryo-EM resolves the structure of the archaeal dsDNA virus HFTV1 from head to tail
authors: Zhang DX; Isupov MN; Davies RM; Schwarzer S; McLaren M; Stuart WS; Gold VA; Oksanen HM; Quax TE; Daum B
one_liner_zh: 该文用冷冻电镜解析古菌病毒HFTV1完整原子结构，涉及衣壳内dsDNA装载与释放的结构变化，但核心是病毒颗粒结构而非TF-DNA结合互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Outnumbering their hosts by at least a factor of 10, viruses are the most common biological entity on Earth, are major drivers of evolution, and greatly impact on the dynamics of our planet’s ecosystems. While viruses infecting bacteria and eukaryotes have been extensively studied, the viruses roaming the archaeal domain remain largely unexplored. In recent years, a growing number of archaeal viruses have been described, revealing a stunningly diverse range of morphologies that appear unique to archaea. Detailed structural studies are paramount to fully understand how archaeal viruses infect their hosts. However, no complete atomic models of archaeal viruses are available to date. Using electron cryo-microscopy, we investigated the structure of the archaeal virus Haloferax tailed virus 1 (HFTV1), which infects the halophile Haloferax gibbonsii LR2-5 originating from the Senegalese salt lake Retba. Through single particle analysis, we achieved near-atomic resolution for the entire set of HFTV1’s structural proteins, enabling the building of a full atomic model of the virion. Comparing the structures of DNA filled and empty capsids, we visualise structural changes occurring upon DNA ejection. By investigating the double-stranded DNA inside the capsid, we elucidate how the genome is spooled upon loading. Furthermore, our structure reveals putative cell-surface receptor-binding and catalytic roles of capsid turret, baseplate, and tail fibre proteins. Together, our data provide new insights into the mechanisms of HFTV1 assembly and infection, unveiling new perspectives on general rules of host-virus interactions in archaea and their evolutionary links to bacterial and eukaryotic viruses.
abstract_zh: 病毒数量至少是其宿主的10倍，是地球上最常见的生物实体，是进化的主要驱动力，并对地球生态系统的动态产生重大影响。虽然感染细菌和真核生物的病毒已被广泛研究，但存在于古菌域中的病毒在很大程度上仍未被探索。近年来，已描述越来越多的古菌病毒，揭示了在古菌中似乎独特的惊人多样的形态。详细的结构研究对于全面理解古菌病毒如何感染其宿主至关重要。然而，迄今为止尚无完整的古菌病毒原子模型。利用冷冻电子显微镜，我们研究了感染源自塞内加尔雷特巴盐湖的嗜盐菌Haloferax gibbonsii LR2-5的古菌病毒Haloferax有尾病毒1（HFTV1）的结构。通过单颗粒分析，我们对HFTV1的全部结构蛋白实现了近原子分辨率，从而能够构建病毒粒子的完整原子模型。通过比较充满DNA和空衣壳的结构，我们观察到了DNA释放时发生的结构变化。通过研究衣壳内的双链DNA，我们阐明了基因组在装载时是如何缠绕的。此外，我们的结构揭示了衣壳塔楼、基板和尾纤维蛋白可能具有的细胞表面受体结合和催化作用。综合来看，我们的数据为HFTV1的组装和感染机制提供了新见解，为古菌中宿主-病毒相互作用的普遍规律及其与细菌和真核病毒的进化联系开辟了新视角。
